stage1.impression: A tight, moody detail of a washroom: a thick pale slab basin floating against vertical dark timber boards, a brushed wall spout above, a pale block (towel) by the wall, and the left third a black void. The light is plausible and warm, but the slab reads as an opaque taupe solid-surface block with a flat, evenly lit front and a hot white oval hole, not lit acrylic glowing through its thickness, and the boards read as smooth CG wood. As it stands a magazine would see a generic hotel-washroom detail, not a specific place; nothing in it says acrylic or says Planet EARF.

blocking_9: The slab must visibly glow warm amber through its 120 mm thickness, brighter toward its lit source and darker away from it, with polished arrises that catch a bright line. Right now the front face is a flat, even 53.
The basin must stop reading as a hot white hole: it should be warm and graded, not near-white (p95 222 now).
The left third (0-230 px) is 88.6 % crushed. It must hold detail or be cropped out.
The towel must read as linen on a brass rod (folds, weave, a rod glint), not as a flat beige block.
The timber boards need real material character (end checks, sheen variation, less saturated orange) so that at 1:1 they are not smooth CG planks.
Some sign of use on the slab (soap, a folded hand towel, a drop of water) so it reads as a lived-in room rather than a showroom.

defects.what: Black void: lum_median 0.2, crush_pct 88.6 over about 32 % of the frame, which breaks the crush rule.
The slab's front face is uniformly lit (profile 53.2/53.2/53.2/53.0/49.2) with no internal glow, gradient or depth. It reads as opaque matte plastic or Corian, not cast smoked acrylic.
The basin is near-white and hot (median 182, p95 222, RGB 212/175/158) and reads as a lit hole or a light box.
The slab's left end and top arris are soft and dull. No polished-edge glow.
There is no under-glow wash on the boards beneath the floating slab (lum 22.7), so the 'floating, lit from within' idea is lost.
The towel is a flat, uniform beige rectangle (lum_range 34) with no folds or weave. A tiny orange glint at about (435, 117) is the only hint of a rod.
The timber boards are smooth and evenly figured, saturated orange-red (RGB 57/29/14), with no checks, nail holes or sheen variation. They read as CG.
The spout is acceptable but soft, with no crisp specular on the brushed steel.
A single bright speck on the slab top near the basin rim, possibly a firefly or an unexplained highlight.

changes.problem: The slab does not glow through its thickness. Its front is a flat, even, opaque taupe.
changes.expected: The front face glows amber and is brighter toward the lit core than at its lower edge. The under-glow spills onto the boards below the slab.

changes.problem: The basin reads as a hot white hole that outshines the slab's glow.
changes.expected: The basin becomes a warm, graded pool that is brightest at the drain and falls off up the bowl. It is no longer the frame's brightest white.

changes.problem: A third of the frame is dead black, which wastes the composition and fails the crush rule.

change.to: target [11.25, 0.25, 0.88], 65 mm (tighter, panned onto the alcove so the doorway void leaves the frame)

changes.expected: The slab, spout and towel fill the frame, and the left edge shows the boards in falloff rather than void. No region larger than a tenth of the frame is more than 50 % crushed.

changes.problem: The slab's arrises are dull, so there is no polished-edge glow, the signature of premium cast acrylic.

evidence.measured: edge step 22 over 11 px: a soft, low-contrast end

change.setting: frosted acrylic roughness (slab faces vs edges)
change.from: a single frosted roughness on all faces
change.to: faces frosted at about 0.35 roughness, with the top surface and the 3 mm arrises polished at about 0.05

changes.expected: A thin bright line runs along the slab's top front arris and left end, and the top shows clean reflections of the boards and spout.

changes.problem: The boards are saturated orange-red, so the room is not 'neutral and warm', and the colour competes with the slab's Smoke amber.

evidence.measured: RGB median 57/29/14 (blue at about a quarter of red)

changes.expected: The timber reads as dark brown rather than orange, and the slab's amber glow becomes the frame's warmest note.

changes.problem: The towel reads as a flat beige block, not linen on a brass rod.

evidence.measured: lum_range 33.9 and no fold shading. The rod is only a 3 px glint.

change.to: a draped linen hand towel with two loose folds and a slub weave bump, hung so about 30 mm of the brass rod shows on each side

changes.expected: Fold shadows and highlights on the towel, and a visible brass rod with a warm specular.

changes.problem: The timber boards are smooth and uniformly figured, which reads as CG at 1:1.

evidence.measured: even grain and a uniform sheen; lum_p5 to p95 only 11 to 57 across the boards

change.to: per-board tone variation (plus or minus 10 %), an oiled satin sheen varied by a low-frequency roughness map, darker end grain and a few checks and nail holes

changes.expected: The boards differ from one another, and the oil sheen picks up the slab's glow unevenly.

changes.problem: The detail has no sign of life, so it reads as a showroom.

evidence.measured: the slab top is empty apart from one unexplained bright speck at about (503, 266)

change.to: a small smoked-glass soap bottle and a folded linen hand towel on the slab's left end, plus a few water droplets near the basin rim. Remove or explain the speck.

changes.expected: The frame reads as a used washroom in a working bar.

out_of_scope.request: Make the slab visibly darker and more smoke-tinted (it reads pale taupe rather than Smoke).
out_of_scope.why: The sink's tint and material are part of the room's design as fixed. Only its glow and finish may change; c1 and c4 may cure most of this.

out_of_scope.request: Put an EARF product in the frame so the colour has a source.
out_of_scope.why: The frame is a sink detail by brief, and the layout is fixed.
